title: Bounded-below continuity of constructible derived internal Hom
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension, and $X$ a scheme whose underlying topological space is Noetherian, meaning that every descending chain of closed subsets stabilizes. Let $\Lambda$ be $\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ or $\underline E$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], put $B=\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and use the ordinary uncompleted derived category $D(\operatorname{Mod}_B)$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], namely the unbounded localization of cochain complexes of $B$-modules at quasi-isomorphisms. Let $K$ be a complex with bounded cohomology constructible in the finite constant local model sense [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: its cohomology vanishes outside a finite interval, and each cohomology sheaf admits a finite constructible stratification with finite constant local models as in [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Let $I$ be a small filtered category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and let $(M_i^\bullet)_{i\in I}$ be a diagram of cochain complexes of $B$-module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with one common termwise lower bound $c\in\mathbf Z$: $M_i^r=0$ for all $i$ and $r<c$. Write $M=\varinjlim_iM_i^\bullet$ for the termwise sheaf colimit. Then the evaluation-induced canonical map
$$
\varinjlim_i R\mathcal Hom_B(K,M_i^\bullet)
\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_B(K,M)
$$
[sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_B)$. On the left, filtered colimit means the exact termwise sheaf colimit of functorial complex representatives of derived internal Hom; equivalently the assertion is that the canonical maps on all cohomology sheaves are isomorphisms. It is independent of quasi-isomorphic choices of representatives. No constructibility or completeness is required of the $M_i^\bullet$.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and the argument of Lemma 6.3.14; the internal-sheaf, filtered-colimit version is an additional local devissage claim, not a verbatim statement of the global direct-sum lemma. See also the local support argument of Lemma 6.7.13.

proof.text: Work in the fixed small-site universe. First fix the coefficient/model identification. A module-object action $B\otimes M\to M$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] is, by the sheafified pointwise tensor of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], precisely a family of bilinear section actions compatible with restrictions; its unit and associativity equations are the sectionwise module axioms of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. This identifies the categories and their linear morphisms. The coequalizer of [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor] imposes the sectionwise relations $bm\otimes n=m\otimes bn$, and hence is the ordinary sheaf tensor over $B$; deriving on the same K-flat models identifies the two relative derived tensors. The currying identity of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], followed by [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] on both sides, gives $\operatorname{Hom}_D(T,R\mathcal Hom(L,N))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_D(T\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}L,N)$. Thus the functorial sheaf-Hom model below is the right adjoint specified in [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. The comparisons between two right adjoints are obtained by transposing their counits; their composites transpose back to the original counits by the triangle identities, so they are mutually inverse and preserve evaluation. No discrete-coefficient substitution or completed tensor is being made. By [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], filtered colimits of module sheaves are exact. Consequently the termwise colimit of complexes commutes with kernels, images, cokernels and cohomology, and preserves objectwise quasi-isomorphisms of diagrams: apply exactness to $0\to\ker d^n\to M^n\to\operatorname{im}d^n\to0$ and $0\to\operatorname{im}d^{n-1}\to\ker d^n\to H^nM\to0$. Use the functorial complex model in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]; its invariance under quasi-isomorphisms and [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] allow us to test each comparison on cohomology sheaves. We will also use diagrams with a common cohomological lower bound, by the following explicit reduction: for any functorial complex model $A_i$ with $H^n(A_i)=0$ for $n<c$, replace it by $T_c A_i$, with zero terms below $c$, term $\operatorname{coker}(d^{c-1})$ in degree $c$, and unchanged terms above $c$. The natural maps $A_i\to T_cA_i$ are quasi-isomorphisms. This operation commutes with filtered colimits by exactness, so every termwise bounded-below comparison we prove also applies to these uniformly cohomologically bounded-below diagrams. In what follows, say a source $A$ has property $P$ if its canonical internal-Hom comparison is an isomorphism for all such diagrams and there is an integer $d_A$, independent of the diagram and $c$, for which $R\mathcal Hom(A,N_i)\in D^{\ge c+d_A}$ whenever $N_i\in D^{\ge c}$.

source.place: Tags 08JA, 08JC: functorial derived Hom; exact filtered sheaf-colimit argument written out here.

proof.text: First prove $P$ with $d_L=0$ for a module sheaf $L$ having a finite constant local model on any scheme $T$. On a model chart, write $L=B_T\otimes_{\underline A}\underline P$, where $A=\mathcal O_E$ or $E$. For $A=E$, row reduction on a finite scalar presentation gives $P\cong E^r$: select a basis of the column span in $E^b$ and extend it to a basis of $E^b$. Thus $L\cong B_T^r$. For $A=\mathcal O_E$, [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] says $A$ is a DVR and PID, hence Noetherian since each ideal is generated by one element. Choose a finite free surjection $A^b\twoheadrightarrow P$. Its kernel is finitely generated by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] and torsion-free as a submodule of $A^b$, so is finite free by [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free]. This gives $0\to A^a\to A^b\to P\to0$. Constant sheafification is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-section-properties], and $B_T\cong\varprojlim_n\underline{A/\pi^n}$ by [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit]; [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] makes $B_T$ flat over $\underline A$. Therefore $[B_T^a\to B_T^b]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$ resolves $L$. The model [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-bounded-free-rhom-model] now computes internal Hom into every target complex bounded below by $c$. Each term is a finite sum of target terms; the differential is $d_Nf-(-1)^nf d_P$. Taking a filtered colimit commutes with these finite sums and with this differential, giving an isomorphism of complexes on the chart, and these Hom complexes vanish in degrees below $c$. The chart restriction of the actual canonical comparison is this calculation, by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. For a chart $f:W\to T$, [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] identifies coefficient pullback with exact inverse image. This pullback is left adjoint to direct image by [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction], so commutes with all small colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. Under the slice-site identification this is precisely the restriction used here. The charts are slice sites by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], with the correct coefficient rings by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. They form a pro-étale cover, hence cover every object after base change; [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism] applied to each cohomology sheaf, then [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology], gives the global comparison and its common bound. For uniformly cohomologically bounded targets use the reduction of step 1. No finite upper bound on the targets or global bound on chart ranks is used.

source.place: Tag 08JI, bounded finite-free Hom model; sites-modules Tags 093J and 093M; Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.8.2(1) for the coefficient limit. Finite scalar-resolution calculation written out.

proof.text: Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be closed with qcqs open complement $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, where the underlying space of $T$ is Noetherian. The condensed open-closed recollement [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-open-closed-recollement] makes $i^*,j^*$ exact and colimit-preserving, gives $Ri^!$ and $Rj_*$ models preserving a common lower bound, and gives the natural support triangle $i_*Ri^!N\to N\to Rj_*j^*N\to i_*Ri^!N[1]$. For a diagram $N_i$ with common lower bound $c$, [det-pe-bounded-continuity-direct-image] applies to $j$ and the complexes $j^*N_i$, and asserts all cohomology-sheaf comparisons for $Rj_*$ are isomorphisms. Step 1 and the cohomology isomorphism criterion turn this into derived continuity of $Rj_*$; the same reasoning, using $T_c$ on the functorial models, applies to any uniformly cohomologically bounded-below diagram on $U$. Apply filtered colimit to the support triangles. Exactness makes their cohomology long sequences exact. Comparing these rows with the support triangle for $N=\varinjlim_iN_i$, the middle and direct-image terms are isomorphic, so the five lemma in the appropriate five-term windows gives $\varinjlim_i i_*Ri^!N_i\cong i_*Ri^!N$. Apply exact colimit-preserving $i^*$ and use $i^*i_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ to obtain $\varinjlim_iRi^!N_i\cong Ri^!N$. All these maps are induced by the original diagram's cocone. Their terms $Ri^!N_i$ remain in $D^{\ge c}$. The cited direct-image theorem needs qcqs, not a finite-dimensional or locally Noetherian scheme; a Noetherian underlying space makes each open subset and each intersection of affine opens quasi-compact, so every scheme and immersion here is qcqs.

source.place: Lemmas 6.3.14 and 6.8.12: bounded-below continuity route; support triangle and filtered-colimit argument made internal here. Stacks proetale Tag 09BM for the open-closed setting.

proof.text: For the closed immersion $i$ of step 3 and a finite constant local model $L$ on $Z$, the closed formula of [lem-sfb-open-closed-internal-hom-formulas] gives $R\mathcal Hom_T(i_*L,N_i)\cong i_*R\mathcal Hom_Z(L,Ri^!N_i)$. By step 3 the diagram $Ri^!N_i$ has common cohomological lower bound $c$ and its colimit is $Ri^!N$. Step 2 on $Z$ computes the colimit of the internal Hom terms and gives them common bound $c$. The exact closed direct image $i_*$ commutes with filtered colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], whose qcqs hypothesis on $T$ was verified in step 3. Thus these identifications give exactly the canonical comparison for $i_*L$, and show $P(i_*L)$ with $d_{i_*L}=0$. Notice that this uses the internal closed formula, not merely an adjunction of global Hom groups.

source.place: Lemma 6.7.13, internal closed-support calculation; no constructibility-preservation conclusion or excellence hypothesis is invoked.

proof.text: If $v:V\hookrightarrow T$ is an open immersion of schemes with Noetherian underlying spaces and a source $A\in D(B_V)$ has $P$ with bound $d_A$, the open formula of [lem-sfb-open-closed-internal-hom-formulas] gives $R\mathcal Hom_T(v_!A,N_i)\cong Rv_*R\mathcal Hom_V(A,v^*N_i)$. The targets $v^*N_i$ have common lower bound $c$ and colimit $v^*N$. The property $P(A)$ identifies the colimit of the internal Hom objects with $R\mathcal Hom_V(A,v^*N)$ and supplies their common lower bound $c+d_A$. The bounded-below direct-image continuity argument of step 3 therefore applies to $Rv_*$ and this diagram, after the explicit functorial truncation of step 1 if necessary. It gives the comparison for $v_!A$. The common bound for the output is still $c+d_A$, because the right derived direct image is represented by bounded-below injective models with that common lower bound in [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-open-closed-recollement]. All uses of this recollement can be made with the reduced closed complement of $v$. Thus $P(v_!A)$ holds with the same $d_A$. In particular step 4 followed by this step covers $v_!t_*L$ for $t$ closed in $V$ and $L$ with a finite constant local model.

source.place: Lemma 6.3.14, preservation by open extension; sheaf-valued adjunction and the lower bound are made explicit.

proof.text: The sources having $P$ are closed under shifts and finite distinguished triangles. Indeed, derived internal Hom sends a triangle in its first variable to a triangle with reversed order, and commutes with shifts, by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. Apply the comparisons to this triangle; the long cohomology sequences [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] remain exact under filtered colimit by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian]. If two comparisons are isomorphisms, [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] applied degree by degree makes the third one an isomorphism, then [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology] gives the derived assertion. To see the colimit rows arise from triangles, represent the fixed source triangle by a chain-map cone: the Hom complex of that cone is the shifted cone of the reversed Hom map. Its terms use only the two corresponding Hom terms and a finite direct sum, so termwise filtered colimit commutes with that cone and its differential. The functorial target models of step 1 then make the cocone maps a morphism of these triangles and their long exact rows. The common-bound condition is also closed: for a source shift $A[n]$ the target Hom shifts by $[-n]$, so $d_{A[n]}=d_A+n$; in a triangle the long exact sequence gives a lower bound for the remaining term by taking the minimum of the two known bounds and, when the rotation introduces a shift, decreasing this minimum by one. Hence the bound still depends only on the finitely many fixed sources, and is independent of the target diagram.

source.place: Tag 08JC (RHom-triangulated), and derived Tags 05RS, 0147; explicit filtered long-exact-sequence/five-lemma argument.

proof.text: For each nonzero constructible cohomology sheaf $H^q(K)$, apply [lem-sfb-finite-model-stratum-filtration]. Every quotient of its finite filtration has the form $v_!t_*L$ handled by steps 4 and 5: the reduced locally closed strata have Noetherian underlying spaces, all open complements are qcqs, and $L$ has precisely the finite constant local model of step 2, including possible $\mathcal O_E$-torsion. Each short exact sequence in the filtration gives a distinguished triangle by [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle]. Step 6 therefore proves $P(H^qK)$. Finally the standard truncations [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] give the triangles $\tau_{\le q-1}K\to\tau_{\le q}K\to H^q(K)[-q]\to\tau_{\le q-1}K[1]$: their last term description follows directly by computing the quotient of consecutive smart truncations. Since $K$ has cohomology in a finite interval $[a,b]$, start with $\tau_{\le a-1}K\cong0$ and end with $\tau_{\le b}K\cong K$. Step 6 along these finitely many triangles proves $P(K)$. The originally given $M_i^\bullet$ satisfy the required common bound $c$, so the requested comparison is an isomorphism. Every map used was natural in the targets and induced by evaluation or the original cocone; thus the resulting comparison is the evaluation-induced map in the statement. Exact filtered colimits preserve all the quasi-isomorphisms used in changing the functorial models (step 1), proving the asserted independence and the equivalent formulation on cohomology sheaves.

split_report.summary: NV checked the topologically Noetherian, ordinary uncompleted integral/rational statement against the local-model definition and Bhatt–Scholze. The proof is written as finite scalar-resolution, internal open/closed adjunction, uniformly bounded-below direct-image continuity and finite sheaf/truncation devissage. Two new statement-only technical lemmas fill genuinely absent generic immersion and topological-filtration inputs. All non-elementary citations have been read with their actual hypotheses; no global-Ext result is silently used for internal Hom. No Lean attachment or Mathlib match was found.
